text.p: German house builder Bien-Haus AG said on Wednesday it was taking over the complete business of Zenker Hausbau GmbH from troubled construction firm Philipp Holzmann AG with effect from December 31.
Bien-Haus said the purchase included Zenker Hausbau Gesellschaft mbH in Austria.
Bien-Haus said in a compulsory statement that it had taken over Zenker because of many synergies between the two businesses, which should lead to the strengthening of their mutual product portfolio.

"With an expected combined turnover volume in 1997 of around 350 million marks in Germany and Austria and an annual building rate of more than 1,200 houses, the Bien-Zenker group will be one of the biggest suppliers of pre-fabricated houses in Europe," the group said.
The statement said the Bien-Zenker group expected good business for the following year and said a significant increase in turnover should lead to an improvement in returns.
Bien-Haus said it expected to pay a dividend at the level of the previous year, 15 marks, despite decreases in turnover.
Bien-Haus had a turnover of 147.3 million marks in 1995 and made profits of 9.1 million marks.
Early last month Holzmann, in the middle of deep restructuring, said it planned a sustained programme of cut-backs and sell-offs to help the firm back into the black.
In 1995 Holzmann's net debt stood at six billion marks and the firm made losses of 443 million marks.
Before the announcement Bien-Haus shares ended up 80 marks at 470 marks in bourse trade and Holzmann shares were up five marks at 355 marks.
